title: Where the energy goes when you brake
examples: Where does the energy go when a bike stops?
Is braking a waste of energy?

explain.say: A moving bike has kinetic energy, motion energy. To stop, that energy must go somewhere, and a brake's whole job is to turn it into heat.

draw.text: Where the energy goes when you brake

explain.say: Most of it, roughly 90 percent here, becomes heat in the rim and pads where they rub. For a brake, this is the useful output, because it is what takes the speed away.
A little goes into warming the tyres and road, and a tiny bit into the squeal you sometimes hear.

Twice the speed means four times the energy to get rid of, which is why fast stops make brakes hot. Electric bikes and cars can do better: they turn some braking energy back into electricity instead of heat.

faq.a: Brakes work by friction, which turns the energy of motion into heat. The faster and heavier you are, the more energy must be turned into heat, so the brakes warm up.

faq.q: Where does the energy go when a bike stops?
faq.a: Almost all of it becomes heat in the brake parts, with small amounts heating the tyres and road and making sound.
asks: What happens to kinetic energy when you stop?

faq.q: Why is braking at high speed harder?
faq.a: Kinetic energy grows with the square of speed. At twice the speed there is four times the energy to turn into heat, and it takes about four times the distance to stop.
asks: Why does speed make stopping harder?

faq.q: Is braking a waste of energy?
faq.a: For an ordinary bike, yes: the energy you built up by pedalling is lost as heat. Electric vehicles use regenerative braking to store some of it again.
The pads and rim can vibrate rapidly as they rub, and those vibrations make sound. It uses only a tiny share of the energy.

facts: Kinetic energy equals half the mass times the speed squared.
Doubling speed makes four times the kinetic energy and about four times the braking distance.

quiz.say: A bike goes from 10 to 20 km/h. How much more energy must the brakes remove to stop it?
quiz.show: A bike goes from 10 to 20 km/h. How much more energy must the brakes remove to stop it?
quiz.why: Kinetic energy depends on speed squared, so double the speed means four times the energy.

wrong.2: More speed always means more energy to remove.
